question: Which customer statements support that conclusion, and how many calls is it based on?

answer.answer_markdown:
**The conclusion rests on 394 individual customer contacts, every one of them traceable back to the exact sentence the customer wrote.** That is 8.9% of the 4,425 contacts in the corpus, and it is the largest single theme. Nothing here is an estimate or a projection: 394 is a count of distinct contacts tagged to the theme "Fraud dispute denied without reviewing the evidence", and the list of their ids is attached to this answer.

The 394 are not a cluster or a one-off incident. They land in all 24 months from July 2024 to June 2026 - the quietest month has 9 and the busiest, November 2025, has 33 - and they span 6 products and 41 states. Customers describe it in 397 distinct wordings, so this is people independently reporting the same experience, not one campaign or one template. It is heaviest on credit cards: 174 of the 394 are credit-card contacts, where the theme accounts for 12.3% of all contacts against 8.9% across the corpus; checking and savings adds 201 at 9.4%.

What the customers actually say is consistent and specific. They are told a claim was denied "for lack of evidence" by a bank that never asked them for any; they are told a provisional credit was reversed as "authorized" with nothing produced to show why; they are pointed back to the merchant instead of shown the records the decision rested on. The recurring complaint is not the outcome - it is that the evidence in the customer's hands, and in the bank's own systems, was never looked at.

For the disputes team, this is the auditable version of the finding: pull these 394 contacts by id, sample the denial letters behind them, and check how many closed on an automated authorization match alone. The fix that this evidence points to is procedural - state in the denial which evidence was reviewed, and give the customer a route to submit what they hold before the case closes, not after.

caveats: This is a complaint corpus: it records the contacts where something went wrong, so it sizes the theme against other complaints, not against all customers or all disputes.
Complaint dates lag the underlying contact, so the most recent weeks are still filling in and month-end counts can move.
Each contact is counted once for the theme; a single customer who wrote in more than once appears more than once.

The theme label is assigned from the customer's own description of the denial, not from the bank's case file, so it reflects what the customer was told rather than what the investigator actually reviewed.

sql.sql: SELECT * FROM themes WHERE theme_id = ?
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1
SELECT tc.call_id, c.date, c.week, c.month, c.region FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id WHERE tc.theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY c.date

SELECT t.driver_category, COUNT(DISTINCT t.call_id) AS n FROM theme_members tm JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = tm.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1 GROUP BY t.driver_category ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT t.driver, t.call_id FROM theme_members tm JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = tm.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1
SELECT w.rank, w.issue_statement, w.call_id, w.date, w.product FROM theme_wordings w JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = w.call_id WHERE w.theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY w.rank LIMIT 12
SELECT c.product AS value, COUNT(*) AS n_slice FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY value
SELECT c.product AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.call_id) AS n FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY value
SELECT DISTINCT c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ?
SELECT c.channel AS value, COUNT(*) AS n_slice FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY value
SELECT c.channel AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.call_id) AS n FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY value
SELECT DISTINCT c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ?
SELECT c.week AS period, COUNT(*) AS n FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY period ORDER BY period
SELECT c.week AS period, c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY period, c.call_id

SELECT m.from_theme, f.name AS from_name, m.into_theme, m.pass, m.reason, m.judged_by, m.created_at FROM theme_merges m JOIN themes f ON f.theme_id = m.from_theme WHERE m.into_theme = ? OR f.effective_theme_id = ? ORDER BY m.created_at, m.from_theme
SELECT * FROM emerging_scores WHERE entity_type = 'theme' AND entity_id = ? AND as_of_week = ?
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT e.evidence_id, e.call_id, c.date, c.month, c.product, c.region, c.region_group, c.channel, c.segment, t.sentiment, e.quote, e.speaker, t.topic_label, t.driver, e.char_start, e.char_end, e.match_kind FROM evidence e JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = e.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id JOIN theme_members tm ON tm.topic_id = t.topic_id WHERE e.verified = 1 AND tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY ABS(t.sentiment) DESC, c.date DESC, e.evidence_id
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1
SELECT c.month AS value, COUNT(*) AS n_slice FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY value
SELECT c.month AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.call_id) AS n FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY value
SELECT DISTINCT c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ?
